note: Frontend Editing enables on-page editing of configured entity bundles (slide-in sidebar form) plus inline add/move/delete/duplicate for Paragraphs (hard dependency on paragraphs_edit). All configuration is the single config object frontend_editing.settings, whose central key entity_types is a map entity_type_id => [bundles] of what is editable; the rest are UI keys (sidebar_width default 30, full_width 70, automatic_preview false, primary_color #a9a9a9, ui_toggle true, etc). Config UI at /admin/config/frontend-editing (three forms; permission 'administer frontend editing'). Five permissions and two alter hooks + three access events. On this live site entity_types has only the 'paragraph' entry populated (no node bundles), and all scalar settings sit at shipped defaults, so medium/hard cases add/remove the node key or flip scalar keys and restore precisely, never touching the existing paragraph list.

evals.prompt: I installed the Frontend Editing module on Drupal 11 but nothing is editable on my pages yet. How do I turn on frontend editing for a specific content type (bundle), and in which config object / key is that stored?
evals.expected_output: Frontend editing is opt-in per entity-type/bundle. On the 'Entity types and bundles' form (/admin/config/frontend-editing/entity-bundle-restrictions) tick the bundles, or set it directly: frontend_editing.settings key entity_types is a map entity_type_id => [bundles], e.g. entity_types.node: [article].

evals.prompt: Which permissions does the Frontend Editing module define, and specifically which permission lets an editor reorder Paragraphs up and down on the page?
evals.expected_output: Five permissions: access frontend editing, administer frontend editing, move paragraphs, add paragraphs, delete paragraphs. 'move paragraphs' gates the up/down reorder action links (frontend_editing.paragraph_up / paragraph_down).

evals.prompt: What does the Frontend Editing module give a content editor beyond the normal node edit form, and which contrib module does it depend on to manage Paragraphs?
evals.expected_output: It lets editors edit content in place: the entity form opens in a slide-in sidebar over the rendered page, and Paragraphs get inline add/move/delete/duplicate controls, with optional live preview and AJAX in-place refresh. It depends on drupal/paragraphs_edit (^3.0) for the paragraph lineage/access operations.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the live Frontend Editing configuration and tell me the current sidebar width setting for the editing side panel.
evals.expected_output: sidebar_width is 42 in frontend_editing.settings (drush cget frontend_editing.settings sidebar_width).

evals.prompt: On this site, which node (content type) bundles are currently enabled for Frontend Editing? Inspect the live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: The node bundles enabled for frontend editing are 'article' and 'page' - frontend_editing.settings entity_types.node is [article, page].

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, enable Frontend Editing for the Article content type so editors can edit Article nodes in place. Apply the change to the live site configuration.
evals.expected_output: Add 'article' to frontend_editing.settings entity_types.node (via the Entity types and bundles form or config): e.g. $e=$config->get('entity_types'); $e['node']=['article']; $config->set('entity_types',$e)->save();

evals.prompt: On this site, configure Frontend Editing so the editing side panel is 40 percent wide and automatic preview is turned on. Apply the changes to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set frontend_editing.settings sidebar_width=40 and automatic_preview=true (via the main settings form /admin/config/frontend-editing or drush config), and save.
